stem.text: Structural isomerism and stereoisomerism should be considered when answering this question.
Which isomer of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{13}\text{OH}$ gives the greatest number of different alkenes when it is dehydrated?

A.alt: CH3CH(CH3)CH(CH3)CH2OH displayed formula: a chain with a CH3 branch drawn above and a CH3 branch drawn below the central carbons, ending in CH2OH

B.alt: CH3CH2CH2CH(OH)CH2CH3 displayed formula: straight six-carbon chain with an OH group drawn below the fourth carbon

C.alt: CH3CH2C(CH3)(OH)CH2CH3 displayed formula: a central carbon with a CH3 drawn above and an OH drawn below, flanked by ethyl groups on each side

D.alt: CH3C(CH3)2CH2CH2OH displayed formula: a central carbon bonded to three CH3 groups (one above, one below, one to the left), then CH2CH2OH
